topic: Central-edge extrema at every center size; Dovgoshey–Rovenska Conjectures 4.1–4.2 and Problem 4.3; corollaries of the perfect-binary-tree classification
title: Refuting Dovgoshey–Rovenska Conjecture 4.2, arXiv:2610.11596v1, Section 4, p. 13: sharp bounds and corollaries of Petrov (2022) and Dovgoshey et al. (2026)

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: We refute Conjecture 4.2 in Section 4, p. 13, of Dovgoshey and Rovenska, arXiv:2610.11596v1, extend their (2026) central-edge bounds, and derive companion corollaries from Petrov's (2022) homogeneous-tree characterization and Dovgoshey et al.'s (2026) perfect-binary-tree theorem. A four-point ultrametric has six central edges against four in a metric. For every n >= 4, the three-central minima are 2 ceil(n/2) over metrics and 2n - 4 + ceil(n/2) over ultrametrics. Conjecture 4.1 is corrected to orders 1 and even; Problem 4.3 has minimum order 1 for k=1, k for even k, and k+1 for odd k >= 3. Earlier counterexamples to Conjecture 4.1 by Love (2023) and Bargetz et al. (2024) are credited. For every feasible pair with n >= 3, the metric edge minimum is (k-1) ceil(n/2). The tree corollaries give the isometry groups and sphere counts of minimum-order ultrametrics, with explicit coverage of the related questions.
summary: Sharp metric central-edge minima at every feasible center size, corrected three-central ultrametric minima, the parity and minimum-order answers to the posing questions, and group and sphere-count corollaries of the prior ultrametric tree theorem.
